question: Desktop release: does the shortcut start macOS on the iGPU in QEMU's window with clipboard, USB redirection and audio, keep the host awake, run until macOS shuts down, and recover the GPU?
behavior_change: rgpusdmacopy=2: writeback is not programmed; a 1 ms poller copies each newly latched scanout surface (or every 100 ms) with SDMA0 RLC0 COPY TILED_SUB_WIND in 256-row bands into one of four buffers and FENCEs seq<<2|buffer into the control page; QEMU (pins-igpu-display-v5) reads that word. DCC/linear surfaces refused; 50 ms hang stops the queue. 460: with rgpusdmacopy=2 the X6000 'or byte [accel+0x1f24],1' (displayable DCC) is NOPed by byte pattern, as Apple's Navi10 personality GPUDCCDisplayable=false, so scanout surfaces carry no DCC. 461: the SDMA ring WPTR is kept monotonic (64-bit), as SDMA 5.x requires; 460 stalled at the first ring wrap after 7 frames. 462: copy hang = SDMA read pointer stuck for 2 s (not 50 ms in flight): Apple's SDMA0 IBs share the engine; 461 stopped after 65 frames inside one. 463: the copy publishes the surface's own format to QEMU (HUBP DCSURF_SURFACE_CONFIG 8 = XRGB8888 desktop, 10 = XRGB2101010 boot); 462 advertised 2101010 for the 8888 desktop, so colours were wrong. 464: the hardware cursor plane (HUBP CURSOR0 regs; ARGB, up to 256x256) is copied by SDMA COPY_LINEAR to region +0x100000 on change or every 100 ms and its position published every poll; QEMU (pins v6) overlays it with dpy_gl_cursor_dmabuf, so the pointer shows again (463 lost it: the copy reads only the primary plane). 465: with ODM and a >=100 Hz host the HiDPI panel keeps 120 Hz by capping its height to fit two pipes (3840x2400@120 needs 1.195 GHz > 1.18 GHz); 464 fell back to 60 Hz for tall windows. 466: supersedes 465 (never run): the HiDPI panel takes the window's exact aspect (3840 x 1080..2880, even heights), 120 Hz where two ODM pipes fit it (up to ~3840x2350), otherwise 60 Hz; no letterbox. Also: the exact 1x mode uses the ODM budget (120 Hz for large windows), even widths (no 8-pixel rounding) with a 16-pixel-aligned copy pitch, and periodic SDMACOPY stats go to the ordinary log so the bounded critical log stays lossless (463/464 recovery failed on CR2 loss). 467: rgpuodm=2: ODM 4:1 (dc+0x244 force_odm_combine_4to1) for virtual streams above two pipes (1.18 GHz), DET1/DET2/DET3 3 segments each with COMPBUF 4, pixel-clock capability 2.36 GHz; the Retina panel is 2 x window / 1.33 (rgpuretina=133), min 3840 wide, shrunk to fit 120 Hz and a 64 MiB buffer. Per-resize critical records (VSINK, geometry, DET) are limited to the first 4 per site: 466's recovery failed again on CR2 loss after ~10 resizes filled the 512-record log. 468: panels wider than 4095 exist only in DisplayID: the EDID base block no longer claims its first (fallback) DTD is native, so macOS can take the DisplayID native size for Retina; 467 got no 2x modes for 4106-5186-wide panels. 469: Retina steps: the window's aspect class (16:9, 16:10, 21:9, 32:9, 3:2, 4:3) and the standard step nearest window/1.33 points; the EDID lists every usable step of every class as a 2x panel (up to 3 DisplayID blocks) under one product per refresh tier, so a resize is a guest mode switch; QEMU (pins v7) keeps the window in the guest mode's aspect. 470: the EDID base block leads with a large DTD (preferred panel at 60 Hz, else 3840x2160@60): 469 had only 1920x1080 there and macOS built no 2x modes. 471: same kext as 470; QEMU pins v8 log each aspect-hold call (470 left the window's aspect hint at 16:9 after a switch to 2560x1600). 472: the aspect class follows the guest's current mode (scanout size), never the window, and only a window-width change picks a new step: 471 oscillated 16:9 <-> 16:10 as QEMU's aspect reshapes fed back into class changes. 473: same kext as 472; QEMU pins v9: the aspect hold's base size is the menu bar height and maximized windows are left alone. 474: same kext as 472/473; QEMU pins v10: no aspect hint, the window snaps to the guest aspect after a drag, smaller minimum size. 475: DET/COMPBUF follow the registers, not a tracked mask: drop DETs, set COMPBUF 13 - 3 per partner, add DETs; a periodic check repairs any mismatch (474 drifted to DET 3x4 with COMPBUF 10 requested: black right side and junk). Window following is off unless rgpufollow=1: the EDID with every step is installed once (stable identity, preferred 2560x1440 Retina) and the user picks the resolution in Displays; QEMU (pins v11) scales it into the window, aspect snap opt-in (RGPU_SNAP_ASPECT=1). 476: same kext as 475; QEMU pins v12 clears the window before drawing the centred picture, so letterbox bars are black. 477: same kext as 475/476; QEMU pins v13 centres the letterboxed picture (texture blit and cursor blend now honour the window offset). 478: same kext as 475-477; QEMU pins v14 attaches a ramfb to the rgpu console so the firmware, OpenCore and boot.efi output show until the iGPU path takes over. 479: same kext as 475-478; iGPU console adds QEMU's vdagent (CONSOLE_VDAGENT=on: guest text clipboard <-> GTK clipboard, QEMU built with gtk_clipboard) and two usb-redir slots on owner-only Unix sockets in the run directory (CONSOLE_USBREDIR=on; tools/rgpu-usb.sh bridges only the usbredirect it spawns, no network listener); fullscreen keeps the aspect (pins v15). Kext: the SDMA copy publishes QEMU's exit stop list (SDMA0 RLC0 RB/IB enable) (it published none, so 478, force-stopped, kept RLC0 enabled and its recovery stayed incomplete). 480: desktop release: the 479 feature set (iGPU console, clipboard, USB redirection, audio) started from a desktop shortcut (tools/raphael-macos.sh); no session limit, runs until macOS shuts down; headless runs hold their own sleep:idle block. 481: the cold display path accepts the platform's DMCUB image held in reset (fresh boots: UEFI boot display loads it through the PSP, windows locked), so the desktop shortcut works right after a reboot.
repeat_policy: Same-boot reuse admitted by the prior run's authorizing recovery receipt; fresh MODE2 and unchanged identity, safety, capture and cleanup gates.
